Jurij pointed me this direction last night, and I am going to take a stab at dissecting IF's E/J trade (JuriJ started this E/J trade analysis back on post # 7 of this journal. I apologize in advance if I am repeating analysis that has already been posted...I wanted to try this without looking at the answers

As anyone who reads my journal knows, I tend to post a lot of charts, in step-by-step order. I do this because it is the only way I can keep it straight in my head.

This analysis only covers the "past" analysis for IF's E/J trade and focuses on finding out why he chose this area to trade. I have a total of 12 charts, so it will take two posts.

I start with drawing FL Boxes on the Daily chart. The next chart will show a detailed view of the area labeled "A":

I notice a break up followed by a break down. This looks like an obvious trick.

The next step is determining which is a FO and which is an engulf. To do this, I ask "What did the breakout @ # 1 react to on the left"? Here is a HTF chart showing the focus area on the left.

The chart below is a close-up of the reaction area. As you can see, the breakout in # 1 is a FO to the MPL of this zone. I think this is highly significant. I think it is this FO to a HTF MPL that allows us to focus on the area below this FO or "trick" when price returns.

If # 1 is a FO, #2 is an engulf

The next step is to find the DP to FO, and ID the area where FOF is created when price engulfs the DP to FO. The area in the green circle is where I will zoom in.

(Continued from post above)

Here is the DP to FO and the EG of the DP to FO. This is newly created FOF.

On the next chart I zoom in to a 1-min chart too look at the FOF zone in detail. I am looking for more tricks being played so I can refine my potential entry. You can see, the FL Box that contains the FOF also has a similar 'trick' being played...a breakout up followed by a breakout down. Just like before, I will determine which is a FO and which is an engulf.

The breakout to the upside (labeled as # 3) looks to be a FO which is very close to the MPL of a tiny engulf that first created the flag box (it broke the demand zone in the swap zone above). Once again, there is a FO (trick) occurring in a MPL zone followed by an engulf.

This FO to an MPL gives additional confidence to look for a trade at or below this level. But first, like before, I need to identify the DP to FO and the EG of the DP to FO: Once again, I am looking for a more defined area of FOF. The chart below identifies this new FOF:

So at this point, we have two tricks being played, and a clear zone with FOF that also corresponds nicely with the HTF QM level. Next step is to look at what FOF is left over in this area (look to see if it has already been spiked/consumed). We can see that it has been spiked...twice.

We know this is the right location, and since the best FOF has already been consumed, I will look to the next (closest) level where fresh orders exist. I will look for the nearest swap zone.

The new swap zone (located just below spike # 1 and spike # 2 is shown with a red FL Box. This is a perfect location for FOF, and it is still located at the HTF QM.

And the final chart shows a bird's eye view of this tiny FOF zone, located exactly at a HTF QM, formed after two tricks were played.

Thank you to everyone who is taking part in this dissection room. It is very helpful. I will do some additional practice on analyzing the approach, as I know this is incredibly important to executing master level trades.

What really stands out to me after dissecting this trade is the concept of price playing 'tricks' in the past. 'Tricks' is really just another way to say fakeout, right?

And we don't want just any fakeout...they happen all the time. We want FO's that occur to the MPL, with a resulting engulf to the opposite side so we know which way price is likely to go (in the direction of the engulf) and we know where price is not likely to FO (back to the MPL, once a FO has already occurred here).

These tricks help us to "zero in" on the important zone of FOF that is likely to react when price returns. The tricks are like road maps that tell us where price has already gone...

Isn't the ultimate goal to find the last available area of FOF within the scope and scale of our trade? Knowing where that last pocket of liquidity exists tells us where price is likely to go before turning..... If we know where price will be attracted (like a magnet to the last pocket of FOF that hasn't been consumed) we know exactly where to enter the market with the least amount of DD.

...And as far as a QM goes...Salivan once wrote he only trades QM's that occur in the right place. Does he mean QM's that have a HH/LL that FO to the MPL? This is the only way to avoid getting stopped out by a Diamond, right?
